newsitem.title: USA: OCC to clarify investment advisory rules for banks.
newsitem.headline: OCC to clarify investment advisory rules for banks.

text.p: The U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency proposed exempting certain services offered by banks from investment advisory rules issued last year.
The agency issued the clarification, defining the term "investment adviser," in January in the form of an interpretive letter.
"This will codify the essence of the letter clarifying what an investment adviser is," an OCC spokesman said. The proposed clarification will be published in the Federal Register on Wednesday.
When the OCC revised its rules governing national banks' fiduciary activities last December, it said a bank was acting as an investment adviser when the bank received a fee for investment advice.
Banks feared that a broad reading of the definition would encompass activities where investment advice was merely incidental to the provision of other services.

For example, simple brokerage activities, bridge loans, municipal finance consulting, real estate asset management services and tax planning advice might create a fiduciary relationship under the rules.
In its interpretive letter and under the proposed regulation, such actvities would be excluded from the definition of adviser under the 1996 investment adviser regulation.
